tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

I'm skipping setup-go since Go is fetched directly (pinned to go1.27.0), and I'm caching desktop/.cache keyed on the fetch-backend hash and platform. For the electron-builder runs, I'm weighing four target combinations: Windows x64, macOS arm64, macOS x64, and Linux x64, noting that the mac config covers both arches while the CLI flag narrows it.

Next I'm working out how electron-builder resolves arch flags against the mac config: whether the CLI `--x64` or `--arm64` overrides the per-target arch lists in the config, or only applies when targets aren't set on the command line.

I'm trying to pin down how electron-builder combines CLI arch flags with the per-target arch lists in the mac config, and whether `--arm64` or `--x64` replaces those lists or only applies when no targets are given on the command line. I think the code path that builds the arch-to-target map is what decides this, so I'm going back over how it handles the empty CLI case.

I'm settling on which macOS runner to use for the x64 build, since macos-13 has been retired, so I'll switch to macos-15-intel and check that it's available when I run it. The fs-xattr addon gets built on the host platform, so the x64 target needs a native x64 runner.

I'm planning the Linux smoke test and expect the Electron binary to fail its SUID sandbox check on ubuntu-24.04, since AppArmor blocks unprivileged user namespaces there. The smoke step only passes the remote-debugging port, so I can't add `--no-sandbox`; I'll instead disable that AppArmor restriction with a sysctl on the runner. I'll also install libnss3-tools and xvfb, then collect the smoke logs and screenshots.

Next I'm looking at the smoke step, which should tee its output into a log file so I can keep it as an artifact, with no screenshots since none are produced. For the release job, I'm planning to download the artifacts on a tag push and create a draft release, uploading only the installers and not the blockmap or update metadata files.

I'm adding a check to the release job that compares the tag version against desktop/package.json and fails if they differ, since mismatched filenames would be confusing. That means checking out the repo in that job first.

I'm checking how the release job handles secrets: if they're empty, such as on fork PRs, I'll set CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY to false through GITHUB_ENV so signing gets skipped cleanly.

I'm making the dist step scrub any empty signing secrets from the environment by unsetting them in the run script, so electron-builder doesn't see blank values.

I'm setting the shell to bash on every step so the Windows runner handles them the same way, and I'm noting that the mac build is unsigned, so the identity stays ad-hoc with auto-discovery turned off. The desktop artifacts also need a predictable unpacked folder for the smoke step, which means win-unpacked, mac-arm64 or mac for x64, and linux-unpacked. Finally, I'm setting a concurrency group keyed on the ref and cancelling any in-progress run.

I'm now looking at the artifact upload paths: the installers from the release folder, meaning the exe, dmg, zip, AppImage and deb files, while leaving the unpacked directories out. I'm naming each upload per matrix entry and planning shorter retention for the installers than for the smoke logs, with the smoke upload set to run even if earlier steps fail.

I'm adding a smoke test step that runs under xvfb on Linux, with the matrix supplying a log prefix per platform, and I'm checking that the mac x64 job runs natively on Intel.

I'm checking whether build.mjs clears desktop/.build, since the fetch-then-build order in the spec depends on that.

name: Desktop

# Builds Moneo Desktop on Windows, macOS and Linux, smoke-tests the packaged app, and on a `v*` tag
# drafts a GitHub release with the installers. Packages are unsigned unless the signing secrets exist.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "desktop/**"
      - "scripts/desktop/**"
      - "next.config.ts"
      - "package*.json"
      - "supabase/migrations/**"
      - ".github/workflows/desktop.yml"
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: desktop-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    name: ${{ matrix.id }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { id: win-x64, runner: windows-latest, builder: "--win --x64" }
          - { id: mac-arm64, runner: macos-14, builder: "--mac --arm64" }
          # macos-13 was retired; macos-15-intel is the remaining Intel runner, so mac-x64 builds
          # and is smoke-tested natively.
          - { id: mac-x64, runner: macos-15-intel, builder: "--mac --x64" }
          - { id: linux-x64, runner: ubuntu-24.04, builder: "--linux --x64" }
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      # No setup-go: fetch-backend.mjs downloads its own pinned Go toolchain into desktop/.cache.
      - run: npm ci

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: desktop/.cache
          key: desktop-cache-${{ matrix.id }}-${{ hashFiles('scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs') }}

      - name: Fetch the native backend
        run: node scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs --platform ${{ matrix.id }}

      - run: npm run desktop:build

      - name: Package
        env:
          CSC_LINK: ${{ secrets.CSC_LINK }}
          CSC_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CSC_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ID }}
          APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_TEAM_ID }}
          WIN_CSC_LINK: ${{ secrets.WIN_CSC_LINK }}
          WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          # Secrets that do not exist arrive as empty strings; unset them so electron-builder
          # treats the build as unsigned.
          for name in CSC_LINK CSC_KEY_PASSWORD APPLE_ID APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD APPLE_TEAM_ID WIN_CSC_LINK WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD; do
            if [ -z "${!name}" ]; then unset "$name"; fi
          done
          if [ -z "${CSC_LINK:-}" ] && [ -z "${WIN_CSC_LINK:-}" ]; then
            export CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false
            echo "No signing certificate: building unsigned packages."
          fi
          npm run desktop:dist -- ${{ matrix.builder }} --publish never

      - name: List packages
        run: ls -la desktop/release

      # The smoke test starts the unpacked app (own temporary home, no cloud calls).
      - name: Linux dependencies for the smoke test
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y xvfb libnss3-tools
          # Ubuntu 24.04 blocks the unprivileged user namespaces Chromium's sandbox needs.
          sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0

      - name: Smoke test
        run: |
          mkdir -p smoke
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = "Linux" ]; then
            xvfb-run -a --server-args="-screen 0 1280x1024x24" npm run desktop:smoke 2>&1 | tee "smoke/smoke-${{ matrix.id }}.log"
          else
            npm run desktop:smoke 2>&1 | tee "smoke/smoke-${{ matrix.id }}.log"
          fi

      - name: Upload installers
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: moneo-desktop-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: |
            desktop/release/*.exe
            desktop/release/*.dmg
            desktop/release/*.zip
            desktop/release/*.AppImage
            desktop/release/*.deb
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Upload smoke logs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: smoke-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: smoke/
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 3

  release:
    name: Draft release
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: moneo-desktop-*
          path: installers
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Draft the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          version=$(node -p "require('./desktop/package.json').version")
          if [ "$TAG" != "v$version" ]; then
            echo "::warning::Tag $TAG does not match desktop/package.json version $version; installer file names carry $version."
          fi
          cd installers
          ls -la
          files=$(find . -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.exe' -o -name '*.dmg' -o -name '*.zip' -o -name '*.AppImage' -o -name '*.deb' \) -printf '%f\n' | sort)
          if [ -z "$files" ]; then echo "::error::No installers were downloaded."; exit 1; fi
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          sha256sum $files > SHA256SUMS.txt
          cat SHA256SUMS.txt
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          gh release create "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --draft --verify-tag \
            --title "Moneo Desktop $TAG" \
            --notes "Moneo Desktop $TAG. Packages are unsigned unless noted; check SHA256SUMS.txt." \
            $files SHA256SUMS.txt

      - name: Linux dependencies for the smoke test

          sudo apt-get install -y xvfb libnss3-tools

          mkdir -p smoke

    name: Draft release
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: moneo-desktop-*
          path: installers
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Draft the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          version=$(node -p "require('./desktop/package.json').version")
          if [ "$TAG" != "v$version" ]; then
            echo "::warning::Tag $TAG does not match desktop/package.json version $version; installer file names carry $version."
          fi

          ls -la
          files=$(find . -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.exe' -o -name '*.dmg' -o -name '*.zip' -o -name '*.AppImage' -o -name '*.deb' \) -printf '%f\n' | sort)

          sha256sum $files > SHA256SUMS.txt
          cat SHA256SUMS.txt
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          gh release create "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --draft --verify-tag \
            --title "Moneo Desktop $TAG" \
            --notes "Moneo Desktop $TAG. Packages are unsigned unless noted; check SHA256SUMS.txt." \
